Anticoagulation is not thrombolysis

A student compares heparin with alteplase after seeing both used in thrombotic disease. The supervising clinician asks which effect most specifically distinguishes alteplase from heparin. Which answer best captures the central pharmacologic difference between the two drugs?

  1. Generation of plasmin to degrade fibrin
  2. Acceleration of antithrombin activity
  3. Reduction of new thrombin generation alone
  4. Inhibition of vitamin K recycling
  5. Blockade of platelet glycoprotein IIb/IIIa
Answer and explanation

Generation of plasmin to degrade fibrin

Alteplase actively promotes fibrin degradation through plasmin generation.

Option explanations

Generation of plasmin to degrade fibrin: Alteplase actively promotes fibrin degradation through plasmin generation.

Acceleration of antithrombin activity: Heparin enhances antithrombin activity.

Reduction of new thrombin generation alone: Anticoagulants mainly limit clot propagation rather than directly catalyzing lysis.

Inhibition of vitamin K recycling: Warfarin inhibits vitamin K recycling.

Blockade of platelet glycoprotein IIb/IIIa: IIb/IIIa blockers are antiplatelet drugs.
